script.problem: A quote isn't the BSB's exact words.
It has 2 sentences. Explanations are 3 to 5 sentences.

terra.problem: Saul being king of Israel is a fact from outside this passage; 1 Samuel 16:14 does not establish it.
The claims that dreams appear in the Bible and that Saul is king of Israel need references outside this passage.
Samuel anointing David is from outside this passage and needs a reference.
Jonathan being Saul's son is a fact from outside this passage and needs a reference.
The passage does not say Saul acted right away or establish that a king accepting good advice is rare.
The passage does not establish that agreement is a nice change for Saul or for kings generally.
Comparing the servant to someone building up the moment suggests a reason for not naming David that the text does not give.
“Wrong dad” uses “wrong” about the baker's answer.
Samuel anointing David is from outside this passage and needs a reference.
“Bread and wine are in the text, so I can mention them” exposes a behind-the-scenes writing rule instead of staying in character.
The text does not list oil or honey, but it does not establish that none made the trip.
The text says Saul loved David very much, but it does not identify this as his first reaction.
The claim that a cupbearer is a job in the Bible needs a reference outside this passage.
The passage does not say Jesse was never invited to move in; it only gives Saul's request concerning David.
The passage does not say David was the most useful person in the palace, or locate this scene in a palace.
